text: Now Abram’s (exalted father) wife Sarai (princess) had borne him no children, but she had an Egyptian (double straits) maidservant named Hagar (flight).

So Sarai (princess) said to Abram (exalted father), “Look now, the LORD {YHWH} has prevented me from bearing children. Please go to my maidservant; perhaps I can build a family by her.” And Abram listened to the voice of Sarai.
So after he had lived in Canaan (lowland) for ten years, his wife Sarai (princess) took her Egyptian (double straits) maidservant Hagar (flight) and gave her to Abram to be his wife.
And he slept with Hagar (flight), and she conceived. But when Hagar realized that she was pregnant, she began to despise her mistress.

Then Sarai (princess) said to Abram (exalted father), “May the wrong done to me be upon you! I delivered my servant into your arms, and ever since she saw that she was pregnant, she has treated me with contempt. May the LORD {YHWH} judge between you and me.”
“Here,” said Abram (exalted father) (princess), “your servant is in your hands. Do whatever you want with her.” Then Sarai treated Hagar so harshly that she fled from her.
Now the angel (Angel) of the LORD {YHWH} found Hagar by a spring of water in the desert—the spring along the road to Shur (wall).
“Hagar (flight), servant of Sarai (princess),” he said, “where have you come from, and where are you going?” “I am running away from my mistress Sarai,” she replied.
So the angel of the LORD {YHWH} told her, “Return to your mistress and submit to her authority.”
Then the angel {YHWH} added, “I will greatly multiply your offspring so that they will be too numerous to count.”
The angel of the LORD {YHWH} proceeded: “Behold, you have conceived and will bear a son. And you shall name him Ishmael (God hears), for the LORD has heard your cry of affliction.
He will be a wild donkey of a man, and his hand will be against everyone, and everyone’s hand against him; he will live in hostility toward all his brothers.”
So Hagar gave this name to the LORD {YHWH} who had spoken to her: “You are the God who sees me {El-Roi}, for she said, “Here I have seen the One who sees me!”
Therefore the well was called Beer-lahai-roi (well of the Living One who sees me). It is located between Kadesh (holy) and Bered (hail).
And Hagar (flight) bore Abram (exalted father) a son, and Abram gave the name Ishmael (God hears) to the son she had borne.
Abram (exalted father) was eighty-six years old when Hagar (flight) bore Ishmael (God hears) to him.
